summary: This note is a clipped collection of LangChain documentation pages (with site navigation boilerplate removed). It covers the Time-weighted vector store retriever, which scores documents by semantic similarity plus a time decay based on hours since last access, with examples of low and high decay rates and virtual time mocking. It also covers the LangChain indexing API, which uses a record manager to avoid duplicate writes and clean up stale vector store content across None, incremental and full deletion modes, and a Providers page listing LangChain's partner and featured community integrations.
one_line: LangChain documentation covering the time-weighted vector store retriever, the indexing API with deletion modes, and the list of integrated providers.
key_facts: The time-weighted retriever scores documents as semantic_similarity + (1.0 - decay_rate) ^ hours_passed.
In the time-weighted retriever, hours_passed refers to hours since the object was last accessed, not since it was created.
A decay rate of 0 means memories never be forgotten, making the retriever equivalent to the vector lookup.
With a decay rate of 0.999 in the example, "hello world" is mostly forgotten and "hello foo" is returned first.
LangChain indexing uses a record manager (RecordManager) that tracks document writes into the vector store.
The record manager stores the document hash, write time, and the source id for each indexed document.
The indexing API deletion modes are None, incremental and full.
In full mode, documents not passed into the indexing function but present in the vectorstore will be deleted.
The incremental mode does not delete source documents that have been deleted, while full mode does.
The indexing API requires vectorstores that support add_documents with ids and delete by ids.
The indexing API should not be used with a store pre-populated independently of the indexing API.
The record manager relies on a time-based mechanism, and the docs say the RecordManager uses higher resolution timestamps.
The Providers page lists partner packages including AI21, Anthropic, Cohere, Groq, MistralAI, Nvidia, OpenAI and Pinecone.
Featured community providers listed are AWS, Hugging Face and Microsoft.
The page footer states Copyright © 2024 LangChain, Inc.
